A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LoSiA and LoSiA-Pro research. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v3 reports original benchmark evaluations, ablations, continual-learning experiments and resource measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains those original experiments and adds fixed-subnet ablation results and quantitative gradient-selection comparisons.

M1.justification: Sensitivity scoring, greedy subnet selection, asynchronous reselection, learning-rate rewarming and LoSiA-Pro's gradient factorization are retained. New Algorithm 2 documents the existing framework rather than establishing an algorithm redesign.

E1.justification: Both versions use MetaMathQA/GSM8K, Magicoder/MBPP, Alpaca-GPT4/MMLU, eight common-sense tasks and the same five-task continual-learning sequence. The added analyses introduce no new dataset, domain or input scenario.

E2.justification: New Appendix Table 6 evaluates random selection and ideal Top-K selection against core-subnet localization for gradient capture. The PEFT comparator membership in the main benchmark tables remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 1 replaces maximum per-task training time in hours with per-token latency; some LLaMA-2 7B latency measurements already appeared in v3's appendix. Added analyses introduce a fixed-subnet control and a gradient-sum diagnostic. Existing training hyperparameters, dataset splits and task metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Table 3 adds an ablation without re-localization, testing whether subnet reselection is necessary. Appendix A.2.1 adds quantitative comparisons of gradient capture across layers and submodules. Existing sensitivity, scheduling, rank, masking and continual-learning analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions explicitly describe single-run experiments in Appendix A.3.1. Neither adds repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The method's sensitivity-uncertainty calculation is not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main benchmark accuracies and continual-learning scores are retained. v4 adds ReLO scores of 42.76 on GSM8K and 43.81 on MMLU, Table 6 gradient sums and additional per-token latency entries. Table 2 changes PiSSA's memory/time from 19.18 GB/10.4 h to 19.46 GB/10.1 h. LoRA's tabulated parameter/memory scaling entries are removed, and Section 4.2 corrects checkpointing qualifications for efficiency results.

T1.justification: Section 3 corrects the subset-training starting model to f0 and explicitly permits rank/output factors equal to 1. Appendix A.1.3 specifies a nonnegative selection matrix. The existing bounds and proof arguments remain essentially unchanged; continual-learning metric formulas are relocated without mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of efficient high-rank subnet adaptation, LoSiA-Pro acceleration, competitive task performance and reduced forgetting. Describing LoSiA-Pro as lossless restates its previously claimed computational equivalence.

C2.justification: v4 interprets the new ReLO ablation as evidence that changing critical parameters require periodic localization, and Table 6 as quantitative support for structured gradient capture. Appendix A.4.1 newly describes LoSiA-Pro as uniquely addressing the activation-memory bottleneck. Section 6's substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.4.3 and Algorithm 2 document optimizer grouping, random subnet initialization, momentum resets and deletion of importance tensors. Existing hardware, software, hyperparameter and code-access information is retained. The new pseudocode's uncertainty update is not fully reconciled with Equation 5.

R1.justification: v4 adds citations to Feng et al.'s KIF (2024) and Recurrent Knowledge Identification and Fusion (2025), while retaining the earlier TASL citation. Related work explicitly discusses KIF; the broader positioning around high-rank PEFT and skill localization remains stable.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the introduction, related work, method explanation and analysis narrative are rewritten, especially the localization and rewarming descriptions. Continual-learning metric definitions move from Appendix A.3.4 into Section 4.4, and acknowledgements and an algorithm subsection are added.

P2.justification: v4 adds Table 6 and Algorithm 2, expands Table 3, reformats Algorithm 1 and changes Table 1's timing column. Figures 10–12 receive revised labels, legends or tick spacing while retaining their plotted findings. The parameter-scaling table loses its LoRA block, and several displays move within the otherwise retained layout.

improvement.justification: The new fixed-subnet ablation and gradient-capture comparison strengthen support for existing design choices, while corrected checkpointing descriptions clarify efficiency reporting. These provide a limited net improvement: main accuracy evidence remains unchanged, LoRA scaling rows are removed, and Algorithm 2 introduces ambiguity in the sensitivity-uncertainty update relative to Equation 5.
